title: VingCard Hotel Key Cards Compatibility Guide
summary: A technical compatibility guide for ASSA ABLOY Global Solutions VingCard hotel lock estates. Covering the Classic, Essence, Signature, Allure and newer Signature RFID / Visionline generations, mobile key via BLE + NFC, chip-family support, Visionline encoder configuration and the Entra / Mobile Access migration path.
heroPoints: VingCard spans 2001–present across four major lock generations. Identify which one is installed before specifying chip.
Visionline is the encoder and credential back-end that binds cards, BLE mobile keys and Entra SDK apps to the same reservation.
Confirm firmware revision on the lock and the Visionline build on the server before committing to a DESFire-native SKU.
imageAlt: VingCard hotel key card compatibility. Classic, Essence, Signature and Allure locks with RFID guest card

brief.label: Best fit
items: Hotels refreshing VingCard-compatible guest card stock without widening into a full access-system change.
Properties comparing baseline compatible cards with branded, eco or premium material upgrades.
Teams preparing a VingCard Mobile Access rollout while still issuing physical guest cards.
Group estates standardising on a single SKU across VingCard Essence, Signature and Allure generations.

brief.label: What to send
items: VingCard lock model (Classic, Essence, Signature RFID, Allure, Signature PMS) or a current guest card sample.
Visionline server version and encoder model. Desktop Encoder, Encoder 1100 or Messenger/RF-Net bridge reference.
Chip-family preference — Classic 1K, Plus or DESFire EV2/EV3 — and whether magstripe is still in active issuance.
Mobile key scope (BLE-only, BLE + NFC (Apple/Google wallet) or card-only) to align the card and credential path.

brief.label: Testing checklist
items: Validate opening on at least two lock generations before scaling the SKU.
Run a full Visionline issue, extend, replace and cancel cycle on a live PMS reservation.
Cross-check the Entra SDK BLE key flow on the same reservation if mobile key is in scope.
Keep one baseline compatible card in scope before moving into premium materials.

sections.title: VingCard lock generations and their native credentials
sections.intro: VingCard (part of ASSA ABLOY Global Solutions) has refreshed its hospitality lock line roughly every four to five years since 2001. The generation on the door dictates which chip family the lock accepts natively and which requires a firmware uplift or a dual-chip card during migration.
paragraphs: Unlike Saflok, VingCard moved to 13.56 MHz HF RFID relatively early, which means most VingCard estates in active use are RFID-native and not magstripe-only. However, the chip family within that 13.56 MHz envelope varies. Early RFID locks were MIFARE Classic 1K only, while the Signature RFID and Allure generations added DESFire and BLE mobile key.
The table below maps the VingCard generations most commonly found in B2B sample requests to their native credential technology and the encoder configuration that usually ships with them.

rows: Now rare in active use; still found in budget estates
First VingCard generation to expose DESFire on firmware lines from ~2013
Wall reader + in-room switch architecture; BLE retrofit available
MIFARE DESFire EV2/EV3 native; Classic fallback
Current front-of-door generation; Mobile Access BLE + NFC
DESFire EV2/EV3 + BLE (Entra SDK) + NFC wallet
Visionline cloud or on-prem + Mobile Access
Supports Apple Wallet and Google Wallet hotel keys

callout.label: Mobile key note
callout.text: If the property plans to roll out Apple Wallet or Google Wallet room keys, the lock must be on Signature PMS / Signature IP or Novel generation with a Mobile Access-certified firmware line. Older Essence and Allure locks require a reader-module retrofit.

sections.title: Chip families and what VingCard readers actually accept
sections.intro: VingCard's HF readers are wide-envelope devices that can authenticate several chip families, but the Visionline server configuration and the lock firmware together decide which ones are issued and trusted in production.
bullets: MIFARE Classic 1K — the broadest compatibility envelope across VingCard RFID generations. Works on Essence, Signature RFID, Allure and (in fallback mode) Signature PMS. VingCard typically reserves sectors 1–3 for access data, with sector 0 kept as manufacturer block.

MIFARE Plus (SE / S / X). Accepted by Signature RFID and Allure in SL1 mode on firmware lines from roughly 2015 onwards; SL3 AES-128 is supported on Signature PMS and Novel generations. Most estates deploy Plus only as a transitional step, not as a long-term target.
MIFARE DESFire EV1/EV2/EV3 — native on Signature PMS, Novel and recent Allure firmware. EV1 is being phased out in favour of EV2/EV3 for the AES-128 originality checks and larger key space.
Magstripe: still supported on some Allure and Signature RFID dual-interface locks; used as a fallback during long migration windows or in mixed estates.

BLE mobile key (Entra SDK). Not a card chip but an app-based credential; binds to the same Visionline reservation. Requires an internet-connected guest device and a Mobile Access-certified lock firmware.
NFC wallet credentials (Apple Wallet, Google Wallet). Emulated DESFire-class credentials presented by a phone to the lock reader; Signature PMS and Novel firmware required.

sections.title: Visionline — the encoder and credential back-end
sections.intro: Visionline is the VingCard platform that glues the PMS to the encoder and the lock estate. Card compatibility is never purely about the chip. It is also about whether Visionline is configured to issue that chip in that property.
bullets: Visionline runs on-premise or in ASSA ABLOY's hosted cloud. Both share the same encoder drivers and card template structure, so a card SKU that works on one deployment type works on the other.
Desktop Encoder: the most common front-desk unit; USB-attached, PC/SC-class, supports Classic, Plus and DESFire encoding subject to Visionline build.
Encoder 1100 — current VingCard desktop encoder with broader chip support and firmware-upgradeable modules; recommended for DESFire EV2/EV3 rollouts.
Messenger / RF-Net: the VingCard online-lock bridge that pushes key updates to locks over an RF mesh; relevant when the estate uses remote key revocation or real-time audit trails.
Entra SDK: the mobile-key software bridge that lets a hospitality app issue a BLE key from the same Visionline reservation that issues a physical card.

Firmware-version dependency: DESFire encoding on older Visionline builds was limited to EV1; EV2/EV3 support and AES-128 session keys require a recent Visionline build. Always confirm the Visionline version before ordering DESFire stock.

sections.title: PMS integration and the Visionline interface
sections.intro: Visionline sits between the PMS and the encoder. PMS integration is usually a driver-layer question. The card chip does not need to know which PMS is in use, but the driver version determines what it will encode.
bullets: Oracle OPERA: the most common VingCard PMS pairing; OPERA 5 and OPERA Cloud both certified against the VingCard Visionline interface.
Mews: integrated via Mews Connector to Visionline; supports batch encoding for group arrivals where Visionline build and encoder firmware permit.

Protel, Agilysys LMS / rGuest, Hotelogix, Cloudbeds and a long tail of regional PMS platforms have Visionline-certified interfaces. The limiting factor is usually the VingCard-side driver revision rather than the PMS.
Cloud PMS platforms typically require a local Visionline agent on the front-desk PC that bridges the cloud PMS to the USB encoder hardware.

Batch encoding: Visionline supports batch encoding for group check-ins, which matters for conference hotels and cruise-line check-in scenarios; encoder throughput is typically 1.5–3 seconds per card including the Visionline round-trip.

sections.title: Mobile Access, BLE and the Entra SDK
sections.intro: VingCard's Mobile Access layer coexists with physical cards, rather than replacing them. A well-designed compatibility plan accounts for guests who opt out of mobile key, lose phone access or arrive as a group that cannot be individually enrolled.
bullets: Mobile Access issues a BLE key from Visionline that the guest's hospitality app presents to the lock. The same reservation can also issue a physical card for the primary and any additional guests.
Entra SDK: the developer-facing SDK that lets a hospitality group embed Mobile Access into its own branded app instead of using the default VingCard app.

NFC wallet: Apple Wallet and Google Wallet hotel keys are supported on Signature PMS and Novel generations with a Mobile Access-certified firmware; the lock reader must be NFC-capable (not all Allure reader modules are).
BLE range tuning: a BLE lock key typically unlocks from 30–60 cm; range above 1 m is deliberately suppressed to avoid walking-past false unlocks.
Fallback card: properties typically keep at least 2–3 physical cards per room in issue stock for guests without a compatible phone, lost-phone recovery and staff access.

sections.title: Card material and thickness — what VingCard readers tolerate
sections.intro: VingCard HF readers are tuned for standard ID-1 card stock but the tolerance window is narrower than Saflok. Premium materials should be pilot-validated on the specific lock firmware before a production order.
bullets: Standard ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 thickness (0.76 mm ± 0.08 mm) is the safe default for all VingCard lock generations.
Thicker cards (1.0–1.2 mm) (common for premium PVC, bamboo or wood cards) work reliably on Allure and Signature PMS but can be marginal on early Essence readers.
Bamboo and wood: acceptable on Allure and newer when the embedded inlay is DESFire EV2/EV3; pilot a production-thickness sample before full rollout.
Transparent or frosted PVC. Supported but loses the primary printed branding surface; usually issued as a secondary or staff card rather than primary guest card.
Anti-metal / metal-edge cards. Not recommended; the shielding or metal layer detunes the HF antenna and produces intermittent reads on Essence and Allure generations.
Dual-interface (magstripe + RFID). Adds roughly 0.05 mm to the card stack; within ISO tolerance but should be validated on the target firmware before scaling.

sections.title: What to validate before scaling a VingCard order
sections.intro: Most VingCard pilots that get scaled too early run into one of three issues: encoder firmware mismatch, chip-family drift between lock generations, or Mobile Access flow regressions after a Visionline upgrade. A disciplined pilot surfaces all three.
bullets: Run a full reservation cycle (issue, extend, replace, cancel) on at least one live PMS reservation per lock generation in scope.
Exercise the Mobile Access flow on the same reservation if the property plans to issue BLE keys; a card-only pilot will miss the BLE regressions that Visionline upgrades most often introduce.
Log Visionline build, encoder firmware and lock firmware for every tested door and keep the log on file. ASSA ABLOY support will ask for all three when a field issue is reported.
Pilot a 100–200 card first production batch before scaling to the full property; most field failures appear in the first 30 days of live issuance.
Do not assume a Plus or DESFire card that works on Signature PMS will work on Essence. Test the chip on the oldest generation in the estate.

faq.question: How do I know which VingCard generation is installed before ordering cards?
faq.answer: The lock escutcheon branding is usually the fastest indicator. Essence has a minimalist round or rectangular reader plate, Allure splits the reader and the handle, Signature PMS carries the Signature branding on the reader face, and Novel has a slim edge-lit reader module. If the property is unsure, the Visionline server reports each connected door's firmware and hardware model. That is the authoritative source.

faq.question: Can a single DESFire EV3 card serve an estate that still has Essence doors?
faq.answer: Not cleanly. Essence readers are Classic-native and do not read DESFire in production use. The three practical options are: a Classic-only SKU that covers both Essence and Signature PMS, a dual-chip card (rare), or staging the rollout (Essence rooms on Classic, Signature PMS rooms on DESFire) during the migration window.

faq.question: Does VingCard Mobile Access replace physical cards?
faq.answer: In practice no. Mobile Access coexists with physical cards and most properties continue to issue at least one physical card per room for guests without compatible phones, lost-phone recovery, staff access and additional occupants. The card order volume typically drops 30–50% in the first two years after Mobile Access launch but does not go to zero.

faq.question: Which encoder should I use for a DESFire EV3 rollout?
faq.answer: The VingCard Encoder 1100 is the current recommendation for DESFire EV2/EV3 rollouts; older Desktop Encoder units on earlier firmware can be limited to DESFire EV1. Always confirm encoder firmware with ASSA ABLOY support before ordering DESFire stock at scale.

faq.question: Will wood or bamboo cards read reliably on Allure and Signature PMS?
faq.answer: On Allure and Signature PMS, yes. Readers are tuned for card-stack thicknesses up to roughly 1.2 mm and the HF antenna tolerance is generous. On older Essence readers, premium-thickness cards can be marginal and should be pilot-validated on the real lock estate before ordering a full batch.

faq.question: Does VingCard use the card UID for authentication?
faq.answer: VingCard uses cryptographic authentication against the chip's sector or application keys rather than treating the UID as the primary credential. The UID appears in the audit trail but is not by itself sufficient to open a lock. A card with the correct UID but wrong sector data will be rejected.

faq.question: What is Entra SDK and when do I need it?
faq.answer: Entra SDK is the ASSA ABLOY developer SDK that lets a hospitality group embed VingCard Mobile Access into its own branded guest app instead of using the default ASSA ABLOY app. It is relevant only when the group runs its own mobile app and wants the BLE key, loyalty program and other features on a single surface. It is not required for card-only or default-app Mobile Access deployments.
